claim: Given a repository root with task manifests (PROJECT_BRAIN_SAME_IDENTITY_TASK_V1), mission files and prerequisite files, and an arbitrary interleaving of choose / claim / execute operations issued by the durable worker identity and by an intruder identity while manifests, missions and prerequisites are edited underneath it, the supervisor (1) chooses only causally-ready tasks (valid manifest for that identity, every prerequisite present and hash-bound, mission file hash-bound, not terminal), highest priority first and smallest task id on ties; (2) lets exactly one identity hold a task lease - a different identity never claims, resumes or executes a leased task and the lease owner never changes; (3) refuses to claim or execute after the manifest or mission drifted from the bound hashes; (4) checkpoints once before the first runtime launch when the manifest asks for it (exit 75, runtime not launched); (5) maps the runtime exit code to COMPLETE (0) / BLOCKED (3,4,5) / FAILED (other) and never launches the runtime again once a task is COMPLETE or FAILED; (6) keeps an append-only, contiguously numbered event log per task and writes one evidence receipt per checkpoint and per runtime attempt.
input_class: Fresh worlds of 2-5 tasks and 2-5 prerequisite files (20 % of referenced prerequisites missing), manifests valid for the worker (88 %) or declaring the intruder, 10 % wrong mission hashes, 15 % wrong prerequisite hashes, 5 % non-zero spend, 4 % wrong schema, 30 % checkpoint-before-runtime; scripts of 6-16 operations: choose, run (claim+execute), bare claim, bare execute, by the worker (85 %) or the intruder, with scripted runtime exit codes (0 / 3-5 / other) and interleaved edits of manifest priority or agent id, mission content, prerequisite content or deletion; 40 % of scripts additionally contain a deliberate takeover sequence (worker leases a task, manifest rewritten to name the intruder, intruder tries claim, execute and run, manifest restored, worker resumes).
scope_limits: NO continuous-OBS context validation: instance roots carry no canonical/CANONICAL_POINTER.json and missions carry no continuous_obs block, so continuous_obs_runtime.validate_context is never exercised (separately measurable)
NO real runtime process: the executor is injected and returns scripted exit codes; the default subprocess executor and the ASTRA launcher are out of scope
NO concurrent-process lock contention: operations are sequential in one process; the inter-process claim lock is not measured
NO lease-expiry semantics: lease_seconds is never exceeded inside an instance
NO guarantee about state files written by anything other than the supervisor itself

declared.lineage: dictionary simulation of the published contract (no file system, no locks, no supervisor code); compares every operation outcome, state view, runtime launch, final state and evidence file name

falsification_condition: Any generated world and script on which an operation outcome, lease owner, runtime launch, state, event log or evidence file differs from the contract: an intruder obtaining a lease, a runtime launch after COMPLETE/FAILED, a claim or execution after manifest or mission drift, a wrong selection order, a missing checkpoint, or an event log that is rewritten or non-contiguous.
history: Component of LONG_HORIZON_MEMORY_AND_CONTINUITY (and the durable-worker half of SUBAGENT_DELEGATION); previously 'verified' only by hand-written single-path scripts. First fresh-instance measurement on 2026-10-14 found one real gap: execute_claimed_task had no terminal-state guard, so a caller that skipped claim_task could relaunch the runtime on a COMPLETE or FAILED task; fixed the same day with a TaskAlreadyTerminal check at the execute entry. The measured module is the live supervisor; the frozen credited copy (same_identity_supervisor_credited_v1.py) still carries the gap and is not re-measured here.
